content_blocks.source_label: UN Food Agency — Global Grain Supply Report (PDF)
content_blocks.raw_text: Global wheat reserves are projected to fall 22% by Q1 2026 due to harvest failures in Ukraine and Argentina. Export disruptions from Black Sea ports have reached 40-year highs. Emergency reserves in importing nations cover only 6 weeks of consumption.

Report from USDA Export Inspection API (2026-05-16):
weekly_inspections[0].week=2025-W43, weekly_inspections[0].wheat_inspected_MT=850000, weekly_inspections[0].vs_prior_week_pct=-34.2, weekly_inspections[1].week=2025-W44, weekly_inspections[1].wheat_inspected_MT=610000, weekly_inspections[1].vs_prior_week_pct=-28.2
Social sentiment analysis (2026-05-16): 1 posts mentioning Commodity Trader Sentiment Feed in last 6 hours. Sentiment score: 0.00 (neutral).

insights.title: Global wheat supply crunch driving futures rally
insights.description: Wheat futures on CBOT surged 13.3% in 5 days (Oct 28-Nov 1, 2025) with volume up 97.6%, while the UN projects a 22% drop in global reserves by Q1 2026 due to harvest failures in Ukraine and Argentina and Black Sea export disruptions at 40-year highs. USDA data shows weekly inspections falling 34.2% and 28.2% in consecutive weeks, confirming tightening supply. The root cause is a combination of adverse weather and geopolitical disruption to key export routes.
insights.root_cause: Harvest failures in Ukraine and Argentina plus Black Sea export disruptions at 40-year highs
insights.forward_implication: If no action is taken, wheat prices will continue to rise, potentially triggering food inflation and social unrest in import-dependent nations with only 6 weeks of emergency reserves.

temporal_signals.change_description: Rose 13.3% over 5 trading days from Oct 28 to Nov 1, 2025
Fell 34.2% in W43 and another 28.2% in W44 compared to prior weeks
